title: Building effective agents
author: Erik S. and Barry Zhang, Anthropic
claims: See What are agents? for the difference between a code-directed workflow and a model-directed agent. See Appendix 2 for tool format, examples, input requirements and tests.
limits: The page carries a later note about changes to the tooling. The workflow distinction applies to this workshop. The article supplies no evidence for this workshop's tests.

title: Writing effective tools for agents with agents
author: Ken Aizawa, Anthropic
claims: See Principles for writing effective tools, especially Choosing the right tools, Returning meaningful context and Prompt-engineering your tool descriptions. The authors recommend task-specific tools, relevant responses and direct error guidance. See Collaborating with agents for held-out evaluations.
limits: Tool effects depend on the model and evaluation. This workshop tests the executor with synthetic calls. It makes no comparative model claim.

title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
author: Prithvi Rajasekaran, Ethan Dixon, Carly Ryan and Jeremy Hadfield, Anthropic
claims: See Context retrieval and agentic search for lightweight references and retrieval on demand. The section describes the trade between retrieval latency and a smaller context load.
limits: The workshop fake model reads each selected source in bounded windows. This is an interface demonstration with synthetic data. It does not establish retrieval quality or latency.

title: What is Durable Execution?
author: Temporal Technologies
claims: See How Durable Execution preserves progress for the persisted Event History and replay. See Transient failures and Permanent failures for examples of errors with different recovery paths.
limits: This describes Temporal. The workshop uses two SQLite commits and a manual retry. It has no replay engine, distributed workflow or service timer.

title: What is a Temporal Activity?
author: Temporal Technologies
claims: In What is a Temporal Activity?, Temporal recommends idempotent Activity functions because attempts can retry. It describes heartbeat details as a way to resume application progress within a retried Activity.
limits: The local example verifies one database write boundary. It does not test Temporal or any external side effect.

title: SQLite transaction control
author: SQLite project
claims: See Transactions for rollback when a connection closes. See Read transactions versus write transactions and DEFERRED, IMMEDIATE, and EXCLUSIVE transactions for one simultaneous write transaction and BEGIN IMMEDIATE behavior.
limits: The workshop checks early process termination, not hardware failure. A stable transaction boundary requires a supported SQLite filesystem and a usable local database.
